title: How Do I Know God Hears My Prayers
paragraphs: Does God Truly Hear Our Prayers?

Few questions are as vital to the Christian life as this: How do I know God hears my prayers? Prayer is foundational to our relationship with God. Yet, at times, we may feel as though our prayers bounce off the ceiling, returning empty. What does Scripture say about God’s attentiveness to our prayers?
The Assurance of God’s Listening Ear
The Bible offers repeated assurances that God not only hears but also cares about the prayers of His children. One of the clearest promises comes from the Apostle John:
And this is the boldness which we have toward him, that, if we ask anything according to his will, he heareth us. - 1 John 5:14 ASV
This verse teaches that God hears every prayer offered in accordance with His will. The phrase “he heareth us” is a strong declaration of God’s ongoing attention and concern for His people.
The Invitation to Call Upon Him
God repeatedly invites us to bring our cares, requests, and thanksgiving to Him:
Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and will show thee great things, and difficult, which thou knowest not. - Jeremiah 33:3 ASV

Here, God not only promises to hear but also to answer and reveal His purposes. Jesus, too, encouraged persistent prayer, comparing God to a loving Father who gives good gifts to His children (see Matthew 7:7-11 ASV).
Barriers to Effective Prayer
While God hears all things, the Bible is clear that certain attitudes or actions can hinder our prayers. For example, unconfessed sin is a significant barrier:
If I regard iniquity in my heart, The Lord will not hear: - Psalm 66:18 ASV

This does not mean God is unaware of our prayers, but that sin disrupts our fellowship with Him, affecting the effectiveness of our prayers. However, through confession and faith in Christ, we are restored:
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. - 1 John 1:9 ASV
The Role of Christ as Our Mediator
Central to the Christian understanding of prayer is the work of Jesus Christ. We approach God not on the basis of our own merit but through Jesus, our High Priest and Mediator:
For there is one God, one mediator also between God and men, himself man, Christ Jesus. - 1 Timothy 2:5 ASV
Because of Christ’s atoning sacrifice, believers have confidence to approach God in prayer:
Let us therefore draw near with boldness unto the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy, and may find grace to help us in time of need. - Hebrews 4:16 ASV
The Holy Spirit Helps Us Pray
Sometimes, we struggle to find the right words or even to know what to pray for. The Bible assures us that God’s Spirit intercedes for us:

And in like manner the Spirit also helpeth our infirmity: for we know not how to pray as we ought; but the Spirit himself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. - Romans 8:26 ASV
Summary and Encouragement

God hears the prayers of His people because of His character, Christ’s work, and the ongoing help of the Holy Spirit. While sin can hinder our fellowship, confession restores it. Even when we feel unheard, we can trust that God’s promise stands firm. Keep praying—He listens, He answers, and He loves you.
